newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch August consumer prices rise 1.9 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Dutch August consumer prices rise 1.9 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The Dutch consumer price index (CPI) fell a provisional 0.1 percent in August from July, giving a 1.9 percent year-on-year rise, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said.
DUTCH CONSUMER PRICE INFLATION Aug 96 July 96 Aug 95
NOTES - Economists had expected the August CPI to rise between 2.0 percent and 2.3 percent year-on-year.
* The provisional July figures of a rise of 0.3 percent month-on-month and 2.1 percent year-on-year have been revised to +0.4 percent m/m and +2.2 percent y/y.
"For the moment, the fall in consumer prices seems to be an incidental development," the CBS said.
Prices for vegetables, fruit and potatoes fell because of favourable weather, while clothes were more expensive due to the introduction of the new winter collection, it said.
Clothes prices were not rising as fast as last year, but some of the price hikes could trickle through in September, the CBS said.
Consumer prices in other categories remained mostly stable.
